subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security policy should OpenClaw apply to externally or plugin-registered recurring agentTurn cron jobs before they can run on an inherited model?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix changes operator consent, shipped cron defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model cost policy, and upgrade behavior, so automation cannot choose the security boundary safely.

options.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
options.body: Make recurring externally/plugin-registered agentTurn jobs require operator-visible activation or approval, add model-cost visibility, and pair any breaking default change with doctor/update migration guidance.

options.title: Narrow model-cost warning only
options.body: Keep current activation semantics but warn or block when a recurring agentTurn job inherits an expensive default model without an explicit job model.

options.title: Split Into Existing Follow-Ups
options.body: Use the related open issues for circuit breakers, budgets, and provenance separately while leaving this issue as the consent/model cluster index.

recommendation.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
recommendation.body: Make recurring externally/plugin-registered agentTurn jobs require operator-visible activation or approval, add model-cost visibility, and pair any breaking default change with doctor/update migration guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cron runtime/model-selection files and recent history point most strongly to Vincent Koc for this policy choice.
